h1: Getting a microbrewery licence in India
title: Microbrewery Licence in India | Craft Beer School
desc: How microbrewery licensing actually works in India: the moving parts, the state by state variation, and where founders get stuck.
teaser: The licence is not one document. It is a stack of approvals from different departments, and every state stacks them differently.
standfirst: No two states license a microbrewery the same way, and the rules keep changing. This guide walks through the process itself, the parts that repeat everywhere, so you know what to ask a local consultant rather than guessing.
sections: Why there is no single Indian microbrewery licence

Alcohol is a state subject in India, not a central one. Each state runs its own excise department, sets its own rules for what counts as a microbrewery, and decides its own fee structure, production caps and renewal cycle. A process that works cleanly in one state can look completely different two states over.

This is the single most important thing to understand before you start: do not plan around another founder's experience in a different state. Get the current rules from your own state excise department or a licensing consultant who works there regularly.

Even neighbouring states with similar economies can differ sharply in how open they are to microbreweries at all, so the first real question is not how to get licensed, but whether your chosen city currently allows the category you want to run.
The pieces that repeat almost everywhere

Even with state variation, most jurisdictions ask for a similar shape of approvals: an excise licence specific to microbreweries, which usually caps annual production and restricts sale to on premise consumption, a separate FSSAI food safety registration, fire and safety clearance, pollution control board consent, and local municipal approvals for the physical premises.

Getting all of these to line up in the right order is often the actual work, more than any single approval being hard to obtain on its own.

Premises approval tends to be the first bottleneck, since many states require the brewing and serving to happen at the same location, and a zoning restriction ruling out alcohol service in a chosen neighbourhood can force a founder back to square one on the property search entirely.

Sequencing is the second common trap. Some approvals require others to already be in hand before they can be applied for, so starting them in the wrong order can add months of waiting that a locally informed consultant would have avoided from day one.
Production caps and what they mean for your plan

Most state microbrewery licences cap annual production at a level well below what a standalone commercial brewery could legally produce, precisely because the licence category is meant for an on premise brewpub model rather than a bottling and distribution business. If your business plan depends on wider retail distribution, a standard microbrewery licence in most states will not get you there, and you likely need contract brewing or a different licence category entirely.

Confirm your state's specific cap and what happens if you exceed it before you commit to any equipment sizing decision.
Budgeting for a process that will change

Fees, timelines and required documents are all reviewed and revised by state governments periodically, sometimes with real impact on a business plan built around the old numbers. Never rely on a fee figure or timeline you read somewhere else, including in an older version of a guide like this one, without checking the current notification.

A licensing consultant who works in your specific state and stays current with amendments is worth the fee for exactly this reason. This is not a process to run entirely from general online research.
What to do before you approach a consultant

Have a clear picture of your proposed premises, your rough production volume and your service model, on premise only or something broader, before your first conversation. A consultant can move faster with these basics settled than starting from an open ended question, and it also helps you compare quotes and timelines from more than one advisor on a like for like basis.

Ask each consultant directly what has changed in the rules over the last year and what is currently causing delays for other applicants. A good local advisor will have a specific, current answer rather than a generic overview.
Treat the process as ongoing, not a one time hurdle

A microbrewery licence usually needs periodic renewal, and the conditions attached to it can be revisited by the excise department over time. Build a working relationship with whoever manages your compliance, whether that is an in house team member or an ongoing consultant arrangement, rather than treating licensing as something you finish once and never think about again.

This ongoing relationship is often what protects a brewery when rules shift with little notice, which happens more often in this sector than founders expect going in.
faqs: Can I use one microbrewery licence process as a template for any Indian state?
No. Alcohol licensing is state controlled, and requirements, fees and production caps differ significantly between states. Always confirm with your specific state's excise department.
Does a microbrewery licence let me sell beer for takeaway or retail?
In most states, no. Microbrewery licences are generally built around on premise consumption at the same location as production. Retail distribution usually needs a different licence category.
How long does the whole process typically take?
It varies significantly by state and by how quickly premises and other approvals fall into place. Ask a local consultant for a realistic timeline rather than assuming a fixed number.
Should I sign a property lease before starting the licensing process?
Generally, confirm zoning and basic suitability for alcohol service first. Signing a long lease before any licensing check is a common and costly mistake.
